title: Logical Tensions in Artificial Intelligence: From Deductive–Inductive Division to Abductive Unification and Dialectical Transformation
content: Artificial intelligence has developed through two historically dominant logical orientations: symbolic AI, centered on explicit representation and deductive validity, and connectionist AI, centered on adaptive learning and inductive generalization. As AI moves from large-scale surface representation toward deeper knowledge organization, this long-standing division becomes a problem of logical architecture. We develop a three-stage account. First, we reinterpret the deductive–inductive divide as a productive logical tension. Second, we propose abduction as a shared architecture for reverse search, forward testing, and revision across symbolic reasoning, human reasoning, selected mechanisms of connectionist learning, and decision making. Within this framework, we distinguish surface representational parameters Ws from latent inferential-structural organization Θ. When Ws underdetermines Θ, and candidate structures are generated, tested, and revised to explain observed regularities, the inverse problem Ws ⇝ Θ has an abductive form. Third, we address the limit of abductive unification: revising hypotheses within a space does not itself explain transformation of the space. Building on Yang’s Boolean Rotation Theorem, we introduce a restricted AI-oriented geometric extension comprising a Q-relative Boolean Isotropic Lift, two-state projective geometry on ℂP1 ≅ S2, an SU(2)-to-SO(3) rotational realization, and a selected great-circle trajectory Γ_B ≅ S1. These constructions distinguish state dynamics from nontrivial structural transformation. In the present framework, dialectical logic is therefore defined in a restricted technical sense as the logic of nontrivial structural transformation. The resulting progression is: Deduction ↔ Induction → Abduction → Dialectical Transformation. We argue that this framework offers a logical route from representation learning toward deeper knowledge dynamics in AI.
